consequence.reason: Evaluates candidates (cv_screening_ranking at initial_screening stage): outcome affects access to employment

opacity.reason: no individual explanations; no model documentation; third-party or unclear provenance

contestability_gap.reason: no appeal channel; no human alternative on request; no named grievance officer

oversight_weakness.reason: reviewers not trained; overrides not logged; AI score seen before reviewer forms own view (anchoring)

red_lines.title: Emotion, affect or personality inferred from face, voice or behaviour
red_lines.basis: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f); policy POL-AI-07.
red_lines.remedy: Remove the module entirely (switching it off in configuration is not enough if scores are still computed or stored).

red_lines.title: Automated rejection in practice: rejections that rest on judgment are not reviewed by a person
red_lines.trigger: automation_level in [auto_archive, auto_reject, fully_automated]; OR auto_reject_hard_requirements without a person reviewing every judgment-based rejection; OR any other level where no person reviews every rejection
red_lines.basis: Policy POL-AI-03 (no consequential decision about a person without meaningful human review); India AI Governance Guidelines 'People First' sutra; GDPR Art. 22 and EU AI Act Art. 26(2) where EU candidates are in scope.
red_lines.remedy: A trained recruiter reviews every rejection that rests on a judgment of ability. Automated rejection is allowed only for documented, verifiable hard requirements, with notice, appeal and audit.

review_requirements.approver: AI Approval Committee + Board Risk Committee

regulatory_classification.eu_ai_act: High-risk (Annex III, point 4: employment, recruitment and selection)
regulatory_classification.eu_ai_act_note: Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 Dec 2027 (Digital Omnibus on AI, in force 27 Jul 2026). Art. 5 prohibitions already apply. Relevant only where EU candidates are in scope; used here as a benchmark.
